title: FORECAST 65 of 65 on its own corpus; FORECAST.LINEAR has no probe
upstream_status_verbatim: W109 sweep (2026-07-12): FORECAST/FORECAST.LINEAR IDENTIFIED and PROMOTED
status_plain: Excel's FORECAST is not the LINEST pipeline: it is a centered plain-double kernel (forward sums to means, one fused loop for the covariance and variance, publish in the intercept form a + b*x). That kernel scores 65 of 65 bit-exact over discovery plus adversarial inputs - 1e12 common offsets, n = 2, near-constant x, constant y, n = 12 irregular, subnormal magnitudes - and OxFunc rerouted forecast_pair_kernel off trend_kernel onto it the same day, so the catalogue reports it as the shipping kernel's score. The 65 rows are FORECAST's: both G3-03 answer corpora declare "function": "FORECAST" (35 rows and 35 rows, five of the latter being #DIV/0! errors, 35 + 30 numeric = 65), and there is no FORECAST.LINEAR probe anywhere in the corpus. FORECAST.LINEAR is named in the promotion headline and shares forecast_pair_kernel, so the figure is inheritable by shared-kernel argument - but that is an inference, not a measurement, and FORECAST.LINEAR's only own row is a pre-fix 2-ULP drift in the 2026-07-10 recon corpus. The source says "over discovery + adversarial"; it does not say held out, and the adversarial rows were designed after the kernel hypothesis, so they are a divergence-design set rather than a blind gate.

substrate: forecast_pair_kernel — centered plain-double SSE2: mx = sum(x)/n, my = sum(y)/n; num = sum((x-mx)(y-my)), den = sum((x-mx)^2) in one fused loop; b = num/den, a = my - b*mx; publish a + b*x
ruled_out: The LINEST pipeline as Excel's FORECAST implementation.
open_question: The 65 rows were not held out and the source does not claim they were. No post-reroute FORECAST.LINEAR figure exists.
reader_warning: FORECAST.LINEAR must not carry 65/65 as a per-surface count. No FORECAST.LINEAR probe exists; the inheritance rests on the two surfaces sharing forecast_pair_kernel.
